title: Bitwidth regression harness and calibration policy for AWQ/GPTQ
creator: Jonah Kim
description: Develop an automated evaluation and calibration harness that detects quality regressions introduced by quantization profiles (int8/int4) across AWQ and GPTQ toolchains and derives per-model/workload thresholds used to gate rollouts. Unlike prior ad-hoc threshold sweeps, this ticket implements a reproducible pipeline: sampling representative prompts, running paired full-precision vs quantized comparisons, computing multi-metric deltas (semantic, lexical, and functional), and exporting a per-profile sensitivity score used by the release gate. The harness will produce human-readable reports and machine-consumable threshold artifacts for the rollout controller.
acceptance_criteria: Pipeline can execute paired evals for a given model+profile and return a sensitivity score in the standardized JSON schema
Calibration job emits a recommended threshold (delta tolerance) per metric and per workload class
Threshold artifacts are consumable by the rollout controller and CI gate (feature flag) for automated canary decisions
Documentation and a reproducible runbook (how to add new models, how to interpret failures) are published to Confluence
At least one example rollout using AWQ int4 and GPTQ int8 demonstrates auto-blocking for regressions above threshold and automatic rollback policy
steps: Define canonical workload classes (short instruction, long context, code, Q&A, summarization) and sample prompt pools
Instrument eval harness to run paired generation and collect token-level and output-level metrics (BLEU/ROUGE, embedding cosine, MRR, perplexity, hallucination flags)
Implement a sensitivity scoring function that weights metrics per workload class and computes a global degradation score
Create calibration routine that sweeps quant profiles and fits threshold recommendations to maintain target user-facing quality (e.g., <=1% embedding drop or <=0.5 ROUGE point)
Integrate threshold artifacts into rollout controller as a JSON policy and add CI checks that fetch and apply the gate
Add alerting for drift: scheduled re-calibration jobs and a signal pipeline to trigger human review when drift or dataset mismatch detected
comments: 2025-02-16 Jonah Kim: Kickoff meeting notes — agreed on workload classes and initial metric set. Action: Asha to prototype paired-run harness by Feb 22.
2025-02-23 Asha Rao: Prototype completed; initial runs on opt-6.7b with AWQ int4 show 2.3% avg embedding cosine drop on summarization workloads. Uploaded raw outputs to s3.
2025-02-25 ML Review by Priya Desai: Suggest adding hallucination check via fact-extraction comparator for Q&A workloads. Also recommend weighting embedding similarity higher for semantic tasks.

2025-02-28 Asha Rao: Incorporated hallucination comparator and recomputed sensitivity. New global sensitivity score for opt-6.7b AWQ-int4 decreased after localized calibration (per-layer bias correction). See PR #1423.
2025-03-03 Product feedback (Luca Martinez): Thresholds look conservative for short-instruction workloads; propose separate tighter thresholds for high-signal short prompts. Marking for iteration.
2025-03-05 Jonah Kim: Met with rollout team to define JSON policy shape and rollback semantics. Decided on soft-fail canary first (alert + manual approval) for one cycle before auto-rollback enabled.
evaluation_summary: Model: opt-6.7b; Quant: AWQ int4; Workload: summarization; Embedding cosine drop: 2.3%; ROUGE-L delta: -0.6; Sensitivity score: 0.27 (threshold target 0.15)
Model: opt-6.7b; Quant: GPTQ int8; Workload: Q&A; MRR delta: -0.9%; Hallucination rate delta: +0.2%; Sensitivity score: 0.09 (within acceptable range)
Model: llama-13b; Quant: AWQ int4; Workload: code generation; Perplexity increase: 4.5%; Functional test failures: 3/120; Sensitivity score: 0.45 (requires mitigation)
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Calibration runs in staging for 24h, generate threshold artifacts
Phase 1: Canary deploy to 5% capacity with soft-fail gating (notify + require manual approval if sensitivity > threshold)
Phase 2: If 3 consecutive canaries pass, enable auto-gate for rollouts below threshold; otherwise pause and open mitigation ticket
Phase 3: Scheduled re-calibration weekly for models with active quantized deployments
decision: Implement sensitivity-based gating with per-workload thresholds. Start with soft-fail canaries for first two model families (opt-6.7b, llama-13b). Iterate thresholds after two weeks of production telemetry.
notes: Calibration must account for distribution shift between eval prompt pools and customer traffic; include drift detection and reweighting
Consider adding low-cost embedding-based prefilter in the runtime to detect high-risk prompts and route to full-precision model when needed
Explore compressing threshold artifacts into a small key-value store for low-latency gating checks
